1) Answer

Short answer: There is strong, multi‑year evidence—in words, laws, votes, and executive actions while he has been Chancellor (since December 8, 2021)—that Olaf Scholz values human rights.

Representative proof points (each with dated, verifiable evidence):
- Explicit UN commitment. In his address to the UN General Assembly on September 20, 2022, Scholz framed Germany’s duty as an “obligation to respect and to defend human rights at all times and in all places,” backed support for the International Criminal Court, called out atrocities in Syria, Iran, Belarus and Russia, and urged China to implement the UN High Commissioner’s recommendations on Xinjiang. ([new-york-un.diplo.de](https://new-york-un.diplo.de/un-en/2553516-2553516?utm_source=openai))
- Leading action at the UN Human Rights Council on Iran. On November 24, 2022, a special session—formally requested by Germany and Iceland—established an independent international fact‑finding mission on human rights violations in Iran during the “Woman, Life, Freedom” protests. This is concrete state practice to protect human rights internationally. ([new-york-un.diplo.de](https://new-york-un.diplo.de/un-en/2563992-2563992?utm_source=openai))
- Implementing business and human‑rights due diligence. Under Scholz’s chancellorship, Germany’s Supply Chain Act (Act on Corporate Due Diligence Obligations in Supply Chains) entered into force on January 1, 2023, obliging covered firms to prevent child labor, forced labor and other abuses in their supply chains. ([bmas.bund.de](https://www.bmas.bund.de/EN/Europe-and-the-World/International/Supply-Chain-Act/supply-chain-act.html?utm_source=openai))
- Expanding civil rights at home. The Self‑Determination Act, passed on April 12, 2024 and in force since November 1, 2024, replaced court‑and‑expert gatekeeping with a rights‑based administrative procedure for legal name and gender changes—explicitly grounded in human dignity and non‑discrimination. ([bundestag.de](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-997580?utm_source=openai))
- Protecting refugees and upholding asylum. By December 31, 2024 and January 31, 2025, Germany hosted roughly 1.16–1.17 million Ukrainians under the EU Temporary Protection Directive, the largest number in the EU—consistent with repeated statements by Scholz that asylum is anchored in Germany’s values. UNHCR data show Germany as one of Europe’s largest refugee‑hosting states. ([ec.europa.eu](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-eurostat-news/w/ddn-20250210-1?utm_source=openai))
- Supporting accountability for grave crimes. Germany has repeatedly backed the ICC and EU human‑rights sanctions. After Alexei Navalny’s death (February 16, 2024), the EU—Germany included—used its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime to list those responsible; Scholz publicly honored Navalny’s courage and condemned Kremlin repression on February 16, 2025. ([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2024/03/22/death-of-alexei-navalny-eu-sanctions-33-individuals-and-two-entities-under-its-global-human-rights-sanctions-regime/?utm_source=openai))
- Pressing China on rights. Beyond UNGA language, Scholz stated during his November 4, 2022 Beijing visit that he raised human‑rights concerns (including Uyghurs in Xinjiang) and emphasized their universality—showing he brings rights issues into high‑stakes diplomacy. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/german-leaders-trip-to-china-raised-more-doubts-than-congratulations/a-63658657?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—formal UN action, domestic rights legislation, implementation of business/human‑rights due diligence, large‑scale refugee protection, and support for international accountability—these are consistent, tangible indicators that Scholz values human rights.

- Source: Federal Foreign Office of Germany (new‑york‑un.diplo.de; auswaertiges‑amt.de)
  Reasoning 1: Primary government source; official records and statements; high institutional accountability.
  Reasoning 2: Carries Scholz’s UNGA speech text and Germany’s explanations at the UN—direct evidence of his positions. ([new-york-un.diplo.de](https://new-york-un.diplo.de/un-en/2553516-2553516?utm_source=openai))

- Source: United Nations Office at Geneva (ungeneva.org)
  Reasoning 1: Primary UN body; authoritative records of Human Rights Council decisions.
  Reasoning 2: Official meeting summary documenting the Iran fact‑finding mission resolution and vote on November 24, 2022. ([ungeneva.org](https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/meeting-summary/2022/11/afternoon-human-rights-council-establishes-fact-finding-mission?utm_source=openai))

([government.is](https://www.government.is/diplomatic-missions/embassy-article/2022/11/24/Human-Rights-Council-adopts-resolution-on-the-human-rights-situation-in-Iran/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: German Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (BMAS) and CSR‑in‑Deutschland (federal portals)
  Reasoning 1: Primary legal/administrative sources; publish authoritative explanations of enacted laws/regulations.
  Reasoning 2: Provide scope, purpose and in‑force date of Germany’s Supply Chain Act as human‑rights due diligence. ([bmas.bund.de](https://www.bmas.bund.de/EN/Europe-and-the-World/International/Supply-Chain-Act/supply-chain-act.html?utm_source=openai))

- Source: German Bundestag (bundestag.de)
  Reasoning 1: Primary parliamentary source; authoritative on legislative process and content.
  Reasoning 2: Records committee and plenary action on the Self‑Determination Act, including its stated rights rationale. ([bundestag.de](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-997580?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Library of Congress, Global Legal Monitor (loc.gov)

  Reasoning 2: Concise, reliable summary of the Self‑Determination Act and its legal effect/in‑force date. ([loc.gov](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-07-09/germany-new-self-id-act-for-transgender-intersex-and-nonbinary-individuals-enacted/?utm_source=openai))

  Reasoning 2: Independent coverage corroborating Scholz’s raising of China rights and final passage of the Self‑Determination Act; UNHCR‑based refugee figures. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/german-leaders-trip-to-china-raised-more-doubts-than-congratulations/a-63658657?utm_source=openai))

  Reasoning 1: Official EU statistics agency; rigorous methodology and documentation.

([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2024/03/22/death-of-alexei-navalny-eu-sanctions-33-individuals-and-two-entities-under-its-global-human-rights-sanctions-regime/?utm_source=openai))


3) Sources I considered NOT TRUSTWORTHY (and did not rely on)

- Source: United World International (uwidata.com)
  Reasoning 1: Advocacy outlet with opaque editorial standards; track record of geopolitical spin; not recognized as a rigorous news source.
  Reasoning 2: Its write‑up on Scholz’s China visit adds little verifiable primary content and risks misframing; better, corroborated sources were available. ([uwidata.com](https://uwidata.com/27468-scholz-visit-to-china-highlights-economic-ties-criticisms-and-us-discontent/?utm_source=openai))

  Reasoning 1: Russian state news agency; state‑aligned messaging and conflicts of interest on human‑rights topics involving Russia.
  Reasoning 2: Used for broad refugee figures but not relied upon due to potential bias; replaced by Eurostat/UNHCR. ([tass.com](https://tass.com/society/1962047?utm_source=openai))

  Reasoning 1: Little-known outlet with unclear editorial controls and limited transparency.
  Reasoning 2: Report on German Gaza aid lacked corroboration from primary EU/German sources; I favored BMZ/EU pages and DW. ([theworldmonitor.com](https://www.theworldmonitor.com/germany-to-increase-humanitarian-aid-to-gaza-by-e50-million/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Anews (anews.com.tr)
  Reasoning 1: Aggregates agency copy with variable quality control; not a primary wire.
  Reasoning 2: For Scholz’s ICC remarks I opted to substantiate via his UNGA text and higher‑quality outlets instead. ([anews.com.tr](https://www.anews.com.tr/world/2023/03/18/scholz-welcomes-putins-icc-arrest-warrant-no-one-is-above-the-law?utm_source=openai))

  Reasoning 2: Irrelevant to proving Scholz’s valuing of rights and unnecessary given robust primary/independent sources. ([sputnikglobe.com](https://sputnikglobe.com/20230323/if-germany-decides-to-arrest-putin-it-will-mean-declaring-war-on-russia-says-medvedev-1108708618.html?utm_source=openai))
